solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shed, important office by the sound of it?

indicators.note: the phrase tells the solver the word for the important office is only spoken, and its sound is entered

parts.note: the throne is the seat, and so the office, of a monarch

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about a garden shed being promoted to some grand office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a noun for a garden hut, but it is a past participle: skin or leaves cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake's skin that has been cast off has been discarded, the past participle of the verb sense.

clue.text: Setter's device, one casting spell on our readers?

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece placed on another sits after it, so the spell-caster follows the readers

parts.note: the readers of this newspaper are readers of The Times
a witch is someone who casts spells

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter muses on a trick that bewitches the newspaper's own readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' seems to mean the crossword compiler; here it is any gadget that sets appliances to come on and off.
explanation.definitionFit: A clockwork or electronic timer that turns a heater or light on at a preset hour is a device for setting things.

clue.text: Controlled squeezes make gas

indicators.note: one word squeezes another when it holds it tightly inside itself

parts.note: to run a business is to control it, so ran means controlled
to do something is to make or carry it out

explanation.surface: Pressure applied in a controlled way produces a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a radioactive noble gas, element 86, given off by granite.

clue.text: Scottish hero in defence, brilliant

parts.note: a wall is a structure built for defence, as round a castle
ace is informal for brilliant or excellent

explanation.surface: Praise for a Scottish patriot who was brilliant at defending his country.
explanation.walkthrough: William Wallace led Scottish resistance to Edward I in the 1290s and is a national hero in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wallace, the thirteenth-century freedom fighter played in Braveheart, is the archetypal patriot of Scotland.

clue.text: Massive loss in the end, heavy defeat

indicators.note: the end of the word loss is its final letter

parts.note: a tonking is British slang for a thrashing or heavy defeat in sport

explanation.surface: A sports report on a huge loss: a crushing defeat at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: STONKING and TONKING are British slang: the first means huge or tremendous, the second a sporting thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses this word for something enormous or tremendous, as in a whopping great lead.

clue.text: Sappers present

definitions.meaning: the Sappers is the nickname of the Royal Engineers, so the Sappers are '...', written as two words
in attendance, as when someone says they were at the scene

explanation.surface: A roll call noting that the army engineers are in attendance.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers; 'the RE' joined up gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is in attendance at an event is said to have been at that place, on the spot.

clue.text: Puzzle always negative?

definitions.meaning: to puzzle someone is to baffle or perplex them
read as ..., never on the plus side, so always minus

explanation.surface: A puzzle whose result keeps coming out below zero.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into NON and PLUS: something that is never plus is always negative.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle someone so they cannot think how to respond is to perplex or puzzle them.

clue.text: Popular opening subject of my autobiography, touching story

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a vent is an opening that lets air or gas out
an autobiography is about the writer, who refers to themself as I
on means touching or resting upon, as a cup on a table

explanation.surface: A writer describes their memoir's popular opening and moving tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' looks like 'moving' describing the story; it is ON, in contact with.
explanation.definitionFit: A made-up tale is a fabrication or fiction, so a story can be something invented.

clue.text: Hoodwink flapper

definitions.meaning: to hoodwink is to dupe or deceive someone
a seabird that flaps its wings, punning on the 1920s sense of a young woman

explanation.surface: Deceive a fashionable young woman of the 1920s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapper' suggests a Jazz Age girl, but here it is simply something that flaps: a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe someone is to trick them, and a common seabird has the same name.

clue.text: Popular novice upstanding in my youth

indicators.note: one group of letters sits in the middle of the word my

parts.note: taken as written
in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: in a down clue, upstanding means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a tiro is a beginner or novice

explanation.surface: Nostalgia: in my youth I was a popular beginner of good character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstanding' looks like praise for the novice, but in a down clue it turns TIRO upwards to ORIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal infancy, the period before one comes of age, is also called this, a sense of youth.

clue.text: Scottish queen ruled, perhaps, English admitted

indicators.note: something admitted is let inside, so one letter goes into the phrase

parts.note: ruled paper has had lines made on it, so ruled is 'made line', hinted by perhaps

explanation.surface: A Scottish queen ruled, with the English admitted to court.
explanation.walkthrough: Madeleine of Valois married James V in 1537 and was briefly Queen of Scotland. 'ruled' seems to mean governed; it is drawn lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The French princess Madeleine of Valois wed James V and was crowned consort of Scotland before dying months later.

clue.text: Shipping lanes are visibly affected, not initially heading westward

indicators.note: in an across answer west is to the left, so the letters read right to left
the first letters of the five words from lanes to not are taken

explanation.surface: A news item about sea lanes being visibly disrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' looks like an instruction to drop a first letter, but 'not' is the last of the words whose initials are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval means relating to ships and a navy, so it describes matters of shipping, used adjectivally.

clue.text: I gasp on spilling wine, dropping one drink

indicators.note: spilt contents scatter, so these letters are thrown into a new order
one letter is dropped from the wine's name

parts.note: Riesling is a white wine grape and its wine
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone gasps as they spill their wine and drop a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilling' rearranges I GASP ON into SINGAPO; 'dropping' removes I from RIESLING, leaving RESLING.
explanation.definitionFit: This gin-based cocktail was created at Raffles Hotel and is a famous mixed drink.

clue.text: Black shaded binding is discarded

parts.note: jet is a deep black colour, from the black mineral

indicators.note: a binding wraps around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: toned means shaded or tinted

explanation.surface: A black-shaded book binding has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'binding' looks like a book's cover in the surface, but it is the containment signal: the shaded word ties round 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo thrown overboard to lighten a ship has been dumped, and the word extends to anything got rid of.

clue.text: Could girl be in difficulty?

definitions.meaning: a girl could be someone's offspring, that is their child or descendant
a problem or point in dispute

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a girl might be in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is the legal sense of children: a daughter is one of a parent's descendants.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter of concern or a problem to be dealt with, and also a person's children in legal language.

clue.text: Town sad, I suspect, about old tree

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round one letter
a suspect account is unreliable, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sad town, I suspect, has worries about an old tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges TOWN SAD I into SATINWOD, and 'about' wraps those letters round O.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical tree, found in India and the West Indies, has lustrous yellowish wood used in cabinet-making.

clue.text: Surrounded by rocks only? Wrong

parts.note: in means surrounded by, as a ship in ice
just means only, as in 'just a minute'
rocks is slang for ice cubes, as in whisky on the rocks

explanation.surface: Someone stranded among rocks alone asks whether that is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' in a bar means with ice, so rocks gives ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfair act is a wrong done to someone, so the noun means a wrong.

clue.text: Gathering pace finally, force trial to go ahead

indicators.note: these two words come before the letter from pace in the answer

parts.note: to jam is to force or wedge something in
a trial is a nuisance or tiresome thing, like a bore

indicators.note: finally points to the very last letter of pace

explanation.surface: A gathering finally picks up pace as forces push a trial forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trial' looks like a court case or test; it is a bore, a tiresome nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A large festive rally, especially of Scouts, is a big gathering of people.

clue.text: Disaster may last centuries, following destruction

indicators.note: letters after destruction are broken apart and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two centuries are CC

explanation.surface: After destruction, a disaster's effects may last for centuries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following destruction' looks like 'after the ruin'; it signals rearranging MAY LAST plus CC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataclysm is a sudden violent upheaval, a calamity on a huge scale.

clue.text: Temple erected in support of sweet native American

indicators.note: in a down answer a support sits below, so these letters come after the sweet

parts.note: choc is short for a chocolate, a sweet

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means the word is stood up and read bottom to top

parts.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia

explanation.surface: A temple built with sweet donations in support of a Native American people.
explanation.walkthrough: WAT is a Buddhist temple, as in Angkor Wat; CHOC is British for a chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Choctaw are an Indigenous people originally of Mississippi and Alabama, so one is a Native American.

clue.text: Drink inspiring oenophiles, primarily?

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: a pint of beer is a drink

indicators.note: primarily points to the opening letter of oenophiles

explanation.surface: A wine that excites wine lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the wine; read as wordplay, a PINT takes in O.
explanation.definitionFit: This grape family gives Pinot Noir and Pinot Grigio, wines prized by connoisseurs.

clue.text: Ecclesiastic punctual, it's implied?

definitions.meaning: a high-ranking churchman such as a bishop
split as ..., before being late, which implies being on time

explanation.surface: A churchman who is, so it seems, always on time.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into PRE and LATE: arriving before late is punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop or archbishop is a senior churchman, a clergyman of high rank.

clue.text: Extremely hungry, so food's eaten when rotten — now all seems hopeless?

indicators.note: rotten food has broken down, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order
the extremes of hungry are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: So hungry that rotten food got eaten: a bad day all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives HY from hungry; 'when rotten' scrambles HY with SO FOODS EATEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a day when everything goes wrong and nothing seems to work out.

clue.text: Secured by ring, second bit of fresh bait

indicators.note: something secured by another thing is held inside it

parts.note: to toll a bell is to ring it

indicators.note: the second letter of the word fresh

explanation.surface: An angler secures fresh bait to a hook by a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bait' looks like the noun for fishing; it is the verb, to goad or provoke online.
explanation.definitionFit: To provoke people deliberately online is to troll them, a sense of bait as a verb.

clue.text: Flier: a through train at last

parts.note: via means by way of or through

indicators.note: the final letter of the word train

explanation.surface: A flier announces a through train arriving at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' looks like a leaflet; it is a bird, and the word is used as a noun for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun the word means a bird, a creature that flies.

clue.text: Deep swimmer

definitions.meaning: low in pitch, as a deep voice
a sea fish, the European sea perch

explanation.surface: Something swimming in the depths.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-pitched voice or note has this name, and so does an edible perch-like fish.

clue.text: More or less on

definitions.meaning: concerning a topic, as a book on birds

explanation.definitionFit: Approximately, as in 'roughly ten', and concerning a subject, as in a talk regarding history.

clue.text: Time-saving preference working

indicators.note: saving here means keeping safe inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: an option is a choice or preference
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A preference for saving time while working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time-saving' reads as one compound adjective, but the hyphen hides two jobs: 'Time' is the piece and 'saving' says the preference holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is running or functioning is in action, a common sense of 'in operation'.

clue.text: Novel was liked — where Capote would have put his foot down?

definitions.text: where Capote would have put his foot down?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take on a new order

explanation.surface: A popular novel by Truman Capote, and where the American author walked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, fitting Capote, but signals the rearrangement. Capote was American, and Americans walk on this, not the pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call the paved path beside a street by this name, where a US writer like Capote stepped.

clue.text: Sign racket backfiring for Brezhnev, say?

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: something that backfires turns back on itself, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a din is a loud racket

explanation.surface: A zodiac sign and a backfiring noise spell trouble for a Soviet leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Leonid Brezhnev led the Soviet Union; 'say' marks him as one example of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet leader's first name was Leonid, so he is an example; it is also a meteor of November.
